speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your symptoms in detail, specifically focusing on the onset, location, and severity of your abdominal pain, as well as the frequency of your vomiting and any associated confusion or neurological changes.

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old female. The patient presents to the emergency department with confusion that started this morning. The patient's husband reports that she initially complained of abdominal pain, diarrhea, and fatigue after eating and has vomited 3 times. The patient has progressively become more confused throughout the day. The patient's past medical history includes morbid obesity, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, a sleeve gastrectomy 1 month ago, and depression with multiple suicide attempts.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) secondary to bariatric surgery.

Given the recent sleeve gastrectomy, history of diabetes, and symptoms of abdominal pain, vomiting, and confusion, I suspect you may have developed Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) from vomiting and dehydration. I need to confirm this with blood work and imaging.

REQUEST TEST: Basic Metabolic Panel (BMP), Serum Ketones, Arterial Blood Gas (ABG), Serum Amylase, Lipase.
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_X-Ray (KUB).
